_comment: One manifest per client install. This file is the ONLY thing that differs
between installs. Everything else (worker code, schema, migrations, the MCP
server) is identical across every client, which is what makes an upgrade
possible without rebuilding by hand.
It lives in the CLIENT's repo, in the CLIENT's account. We keep a copy only
while engaged, and it contains no secrets: every credential is a reference
to a secret store, never a value.

infrastructure._comment: Client-owned. We hold a scoped, expiring token and nothing else.

_token_scopes: The API token the client issues us needs exactly these, no more:
Account > Workers R2 Storage: Edit   (only if r2_bucket is set)
Vectorize Edit was verified on 2026-08-23 for index creation and every
metadata index. A separate named Wrangler profile is only a fallback
for an older token that does not carry that permission; `brain doctor`
prints its exact profile sign-in step and confirms this manifest account.
The account must ALSO be on the Workers Paid plan, 5 USD a month minimum.
Free can create Vectorize, but its vector, daily-write, and Worker CPU limits are prototype-scale. Paid is the supported production baseline.
cloudflare._vectorize_index_comment: The index NAME, not an id. Leave it out (or leave the placeholder) and provision derives <slug>-brain. Two installs must never share one name: the second would adopt the first's vectors.
_drain_cron_comment: Moves newly ingested chunks from D1 into Vectorize. It exists because
there is no transaction across the two, so a chunk lands in D1 first and
is embedded after. Until it drains, that chunk is findable by keyword and
invisible to semantic search, and NOTHING else reports that: both systems
are up and every health probe passes. `brain health` reads the backlog.
Every minute, not every five. The drain advances roughly one batch per
Vectorize CONFIRMATION, not per tick, so the tick rate sets the ceiling
on how fast a backlog clears. Measured on a real install: */5 sustained
about 20 vectors a minute, which is over four days for a first load of
125k chunks. Every minute sustained about 59, which is closer to one.
Raising it cannot raise the embedding bill. A tick that arrives before
Vectorize has confirmed the previous changeset returns immediately, on
one describe() call, having embedded nothing. The extra ticks are no-ops
and the work done per confirmation is unchanged. What changes is only
how long a new install spends looking empty.

_comment: Migration and temporary rollback compatibility only. It is not a higher
product tier and it is not enabled automatically at any corpus size.
D1 plus Vectorize is the standard architecture every client installs.
A different backend requires a measured eval failure, a diagnosed cause
and an explicit architecture decision. Chunk count alone is not a trigger.
supabase.trigger_for_enabling: no automatic trigger; migration or temporary rollback only
supabase.comfortable_below: not defined; prove retrieval quality with the full eval set

corpora._comment: Which sources this install ingests. Each maps to a connector.

_comment: Any mailbox that speaks IMAP: Yahoo, Fastmail, iCloud, a mailbox your
host gave you. `brain connect imap <manifest> --host <h> --user <you>`
asks for the password hidden and stores it in YOUR OWN Keychain or
Windows DPAPI store, under an item named for IMAP, not for Google. Most
providers need an APP PASSWORD rather than the account password.
Read-only at the protocol level, so nothing is marked as read. Inbox
and Sent are read; Junk, Trash, Drafts, All Mail and Archive are not;
a folder whose purpose cannot be identified is left alone too. Every
folder is named in the run with the true reason it was or was not read.
Incremental through UIDVALIDITY plus a per-folder UID watermark; when
the server changes UIDVALIDITY you are told and the folder is re-read.
Bulk mail is filtered LOCALLY on message headers, needing two
independent signals. That is weaker than Gmail's server-side category
classifier and is not the same thing. Deletions in the mailbox are NOT
propagated. `brain disconnect imap` forgets the password.
Mac-only live message capture from Messages.app (chat.db); there is no
Windows or Linux path. `brain connect imessage` verifies the Full Disk
Access grant with a real read, runs the initial history load, then
installs an every-minute capture LaunchAgent (override the tick with
operations.imessage_capture_cron). SMS rides in when Text Message
Forwarding is on and is tagged sms. `brain disconnect imessage` undoes it.
Zoom cloud-recording transcripts. Requires a PAID (Licensed) Zoom seat:
the free Basic tier cannot cloud record at all, so it can never produce
a transcript, and `brain connect zoom` refuses it rather than connecting
into a silent nothing. You create a Server-to-Server OAuth app in YOUR
OWN Zoom account with the cloud_recording:read:admin scope; connect
verifies it live, writes its four values as secrets on YOUR OWN worker,
and proves the webhook answers Zoom's validation before you paste the
URL into Zoom. NEW recordings only: nothing backfills older ones.
`brain disconnect zoom` removes the secrets so deliveries are refused.
Read-only conversation history through the owner's own Slack app.
OAuth credentials stay in the local provider credential store and are
never placed in this manifest. Optionally restrict the load to exact
channel_ids. Removed-message authority remains an explicit gap.
Read-only pages explicitly shared with the owner's Notion integration.
OAuth credentials stay in the local provider credential store. Pages
outside the integration share boundary cannot be inventoried.
QuickBooks Online runtime queries are read-only, but Intuit's one
Accounting OAuth scope grants broader read and update permission.
This release connects sandbox companies only. Register the exact
http://localhost:47812/ redirect shown by the technician command.
OAuth credentials and the selected company id stay in the local
provider credential store. Disconnect retains imported documents;
removal needs a separately reviewed forget preview.
Microsoft 365 Outlook plus selected OneDrive or SharePoint drives.
Graph delta links carry exact message and file tombstones. Add exact
drive_ids or site_ids after reviewing the tenant selection.

dropbox._comment: Recursive Dropbox body sync with exact cursor tombstones.

hubspot._comment: Read-only contacts, companies, and deals. Hard deletion remains an explicit gap.

upload._comment: Manual drop zone. Setup enables and records it after a folder is chosen; until then there is no folder to load.

_comment: A folder on this Mac that reloads itself on a schedule, so 'export it
into this folder and forget about it' is actually true for a folder
that is not inside Google Drive. Point it at wherever the client drops
things: a WhatsApp or SMS export, a saved .vtt meeting transcript, a
mail archive, scanned paperwork.
Install it with `brain schedule <manifest> --install --folder`. Each
tick runs the ordinary local ingest, so it reuses that command's
content-hash resume state: a new file is added, a changed file is
re-sent, an unchanged file costs one read, and a file that is gone is
removed through the same aggregate removal plan Drive uses. The path
must be absolute. Tick with operations.folder_ingest_cron.
Plaid is the reviewed bank-feed profile. Keep this off until the
client has a Plaid account, Sandbox credentials have been entered
through the hidden prompt, the independent bank wrapping key is in
reviewed owner recovery custody, and the exact return and webhook URLs are
registered in that Plaid environment. Credentials never go here.
The account holder completes Link themselves. This brain requests only
read-only Transactions and never sees bank login credentials. Scheduled
reconciliation remains active because webhooks are not a sole source of truth.
Live capture through a paired linked device, and OPT-IN twice over:
this flag, plus --accept-risk on `brain connect whatsapp <manifest>`.
Pairing uses an unofficial client, which is a terms-of-service gray area
with a small but real ban risk, and the history it collects at link time
is only what the phone chooses to transfer. Installing it needs macOS;
Windows supervision is not built. The per-chat Export chat path needs no
flag, no daemon and carries no such risk. `brain disconnect whatsapp`
undoes it. Knobs: operations.whatsapp_drain_cron, whatsapp_daemon_path,
whatsapp_data_dir.

retrieval._comment: answer_model runs through the CLIENT's own Cloudflare Workers AI binding, so no external model credential is required.

safety._comment: Non-negotiable defaults. The scanner is what makes 'we store nothing dangerous' true rather than aspirational.

ocr._comment: Read scanned PDFs by sending each page image to a vision model through THIS brain's own Workers AI binding. OFF by default on purpose: it spends money on the client's own Cloudflare account, once per scanned page, and nobody should discover that after the fact. Every page must atomically reserve a conservative amount from the daily estimated-spend budget, and every document read this way is MARKED as OCR so an answer resting on it says so.
ocr._model_note: Must be a Cloudflare @cf/ model. OCR refuses anything else rather than send a picture of a client document to a provider this manifest does not name.

_ingest_cron_comment: On macOS this installs as a per-user LaunchAgent and runs Google Drive
normally incrementally, with periodic and policy-triggered full comparisons.
The plist contains no credentials. Calendar times use
the Mac's local timezone, which the installer compares with client.timezone.
Standard brain setup fills admin_key_secret with a deterministic, non-secret
macOS Keychain locator before generating a key. An existing legacy adjacent
.brain-admin-key is preserved. Windows uses a DPAPI-protected adjacent file;
Linux uses an owner-only adjacent file. Never put the key itself here.
brain secrets updates and verifies that declared durable location.
google_token_store persists auto, keychain or file for unattended runs.

_comment: Filled from section 6 of the intake questionnaire, in the CLIENT'S OWN
WORDS. Do not tidy them into better English: 'why did we stop using
those guys' retrieves differently than 'vendor termination rationale',
and theirs is the phrasing that has to work.
These do double duty. The acceptance suite uses them as retrieval probes,
so a passing install is one that answers THIS client's questions rather
than generic ones. And they are the kickoff script: the first thing the
client sees is their own ten questions answered with citations.
_expected_to_fail_note: Two questions the client predicts it will get wrong, captured at intake.
Shown at kickoff alongside the wins. A tool that says what it does not
know is worth more than one that always sounds confident, and predicting
the misses in advance turns the gap list into honesty rather than failure.

_comment: The priority slice goes in FIRST and gets proven before the long tail
streams in behind it. Do NOT ingest chronologically: order by likely
answer value, usually the last 12 to 24 months plus every meeting
transcript. A default tuned for steady state quietly ruins the first
impression, which is the one that decides whether they trust it.

priority_slice.note: from intake question 2.4, the single folder that would already be worth it

_comment: As of v0.1 everyone with access sees everything indexed. Document-level
permissions are NOT built. Any client with employees who must not share
sight of every document is out of scope until ACLs ship. This field exists
so the limitation is explicit in the install record rather than discovered
later.

handoff._comment: On handoff, the client revokes our token and this records the date. After that we hold nothing.
